transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thanks for fitting me in. Um... well, I guess what brought me in is... people keep saying I’m not listening to them. Which, I mean, I feel terrible about, because I really do try to be a good listener. 

But my supervisor at the plant, or my wife, they’ll be talking straight to me, and... I don't know, a minute later I just realize I only caught maybe half of it. And then I have to ask them to say it again. It's probably just me being a little too distracted with work and everything, you know? But they get pretty frustrated, so I figured I should come see someone. I hope that's a good enough reason to be here... does that make sense?
How long have you been experiencing these difficulties with paying attention?

Um, well... I guess it really hasn't been this bad for my whole life or anything. It's mostly just been the last... maybe two years and two months? Give or take? 

That’s, um, that's right around when my wife started working outside the home. So suddenly I had to handle a lot more of the daily schedule on my own, which I was totally happy to do! I really want to pull my weight, you know? I try really hard to be supportive. But... yeah, trying to keep track of all the new schedules and everything on my own, that's when the listening thing got really noticeable. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm just making excuses or complaining about my wife working, because I'm definitely not. Is it normal for things to get a little harder to manage like that when your routine changes?
When you notice yourself zoning out or missing what people say, are there specific worries or thoughts running through your mind?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I'm not sitting there worrying about anything specific, like money or... or being anxious or anything like that. I really don't want you to think I'm, like, ignoring them on purpose because I'm stuck in my own head. 

It's more like... my mind just sort of goes blank, or maybe it just hops over to something completely random. Like, I'll be looking right at them, and then suddenly I'm thinking about a piece of machinery at the plant that needs a new belt, or... or wondering if I took the trash out. It's just silly little things, nothing serious. I try so hard to push those thoughts away and focus back on them, I really do. I know I should be paying better attention. Does that sound like a normal thing that happens to people sometimes?
Looking back to when you were in elementary or middle school, did you ever have trouble with daydreaming or paying attention in class?

Um, well... I guess I was a little bit of a handful back then, maybe? I mean, I wasn't a bad kid or anything, I promise! I always wanted to do a good job. But, um... yeah, even back in elementary school, my teachers were always having to move my desk around. 

I just had a really hard time staying in my seat, you know? I'd get a little antsy. And sometimes I'd get so excited about knowing the answer that I'd just blurt it out before they even called on me. I really didn't mean to be disrespectful, I just... I don't know, it just slipped out. And I guess I got into trouble a few times for kind of hovering over other kids and getting involved in what they were doing instead of my own work. That was all before middle school, mostly. I really tried to be good, though, I swear. Is it pretty common for kids to be a little squirmy and eager like that?
Nowadays, do you find yourself feeling physically restless or having trouble sitting still?

Um, well... I guess I do still get a little bit fidgety sometimes. I mean, working at the plant, I'm on my feet and moving around all day, which is great, so it's not usually an issue there! I'm a really hard worker. But, um... yeah, if I *have* to sit still for a while, like if we have a long safety meeting or something, it gets a little tough. 

I try my absolute best to just sit quietly and not bother anyone around me, I really do. But... I don't know, it's like this pressure just starts building up inside my chest and my legs. It gets to the point where it feels like I've got to move or do something right that second, or... or I'll just crawl out of my skin. I always try to hide it, though, so I don't look impatient or rude to whoever is talking. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad listener or anything. Is it normal for a guy my age to still get that uncomfortable just from having to sit in a chair?
Nowadays, do you ever find yourself interrupting people or finishing their sentences before they're done talking?

Um, gosh... I guess I do sometimes. I really try not to, though! I swear I'm not trying to be rude or talk over anyone. I think I just get so eager to help out or answer that I jump the gun a little bit. 

Like, um, at work during our shift meetings, the supervisor will be asking a question, and I just sort of... blurt out the answer before he's even finished asking it. Sometimes I'm already halfway through talking before I even realize I didn't let him get to the most important part of what he was trying to say. I always feel terrible right after, and I apologize right away. I just want to show that I'm paying attention and I know my stuff, you know? I really hope he doesn't think I'm trying to be a know-it-all or that I don't respect him. Do you think people understand that sometimes it's just enthusiasm, and not meant to be disrespectful?
